sections.title: Overview
sections.body: Charging & Allocations implements Cluster F's two-stage cost-flow model. The module's left rail has four sections — **Inter-service Distribution**, **BTC Profiles**, **Location Cost Rollup**, and **Reporting** — each addressable as `/charging?section=distribution|btc|rollup|reports`. Stage 1 routes own-cost between chargeable entities along a DAG of percentage-weighted edges per `[F-S1-01..08]`; Stage 2 allocates each entity's effective cost across charging locations through Business-Transfer Charging (BTC) profiles per `[F-S2-01..08]`. Stage 1 distribution versions are **effective-dated** (FD-3): each version carries an `active_from` date, a version-level rationale, and an immutable-on-activate state; resolution is by date alone, with no yearly cadence assumption. Stage 2 BTC profiles remain year-scoped. Both stages support scenario-scoped forks for the What-If simulator without disturbing canonical state.

sections.title: Inter-service Distribution (Stage 1)
sections.body:
**Purpose:** route an entity's own cost to (a) downstream services it powers and (b) the business directly, with whatever stays neither distributed nor sent-to-business shown as **self-retained**.

**Sum rule (preserved through FD-3):** for each entity, `to_business_pct + Σ(outgoing edge percentages) ≤ 100`. The remainder is the derived self-retained share, displayed in the editor's KPI strip.

**Effective-dated versioning per `[F-S1-02]`:** distribution edges live inside a **DistributionVersion** — a header row carrying an `active_from` date, a `status` (draft / active), a `rationale`, and an `origin` (blank / copy_active / copy_prior). The version in force on any given date is the one with the latest `active_from ≤ that date`. Active versions are immutable; edits scope to drafts only. There is no `baseline` / `forecast` / `actuals` string axis — Stage 1 is now a single effective-dated production chain plus optional scenario-scoped forks.

**Default view:** the cross-entity list at `?section=distribution` shows every Stage 1 edge for the currently-in-force production version, with the version label and `active_from` shown at the top. The version selector lets controllers preview any past or future version; drafts are tagged visibly. Filters: Source type (Project / Offering / Internal Service) and free-text Search across source and destination identifiers and names.

**Version creation per `[F-S1-04]`:** controllers create a new draft via the **Create version** CTA, choosing one of three origins — *blank* (empty draft), *copy-active* (pre-filled from the currently-in-force version), or *copy-prior* (pre-filled from any selected historical version). Version-level `rationale` is required at activation. Future-dated drafts are first-class per `[F-S1-03]` — set `active_from` to a future date and the version stays dormant until then while the current version remains authoritative.

**Per-entity Stage 1 view per `[F-S1-06]`:** click any source entity to open its dedicated surface — outbound edges, to-business %, self-retained residual, effective cost, per-edge rationale, and the version timeline for that entity. This is the natural mental-model unit for an accountable owner.

**Single-entity editor:** within a draft version, the entity-scoped editor has three areas: a *Distribution shape* card (To-Business % editor + Distributed Σ + Self-retained derived), an *Outgoing edges* table with inline edit/delete and **per-edge rationale field per `[F-S1-05]`**, and an *Add destination* dialog with destination type filter, search, percentage input, and a live headroom indicator. Editing against an active version is disabled — controllers must create a new draft first.

**Diff report per `[F-S1-07]`:** the **Compare versions** view runs an identity-based diff between two versions, defaulting to a version vs the one it supersedes by effective date (not by upload recency). Edges are bucketed into added / removed / changed with old→new % + rationale deltas.

**Activation per `[F-S1-08]`:** the activate action takes a single `active_from` date applied to the whole version — per-edge independent activation is rejected by design. Duplicate `active_from` within the production chain is blocked at write time.

**Cycle detection (preserved through FD-3):** save is hard-blocked if the new edge would close a cycle within the version's edge set. The 409 response carries the cycle chain (e.g. `IT00S042 → … → IT00S042`) which the dialog renders as a path so the user knows where the loop lives.

**Role gating per `[F-AC-01]`:** controllers always have edit rights for both version-management and edge mutations; other roles need an explicit `RolePermissionGrant` on `entity_type='distribution'`. Read access is open to all logged-in roles.

sections.title: BTC Profiles (Stage 2)
sections.body:
**Purpose:** allocate each chargeable entity's effective Stage 1 cost across charging locations. The seed ships ~27 profiles (15 manual + 12 automatic) for a year.

**Two modes per `[F-S2-01]`:**
- **Manual** — controller authors lines (charging location + percentage) by hand; the sum-to-100 gate per `[F-S2-02]` blocks save until `|Σ − 100| < 0.01`.
- **Automatic** — the profile snapshots from the User Measurement (UM) matrix for a chosen S-code per `[F-S2-03]`. The UM matrix is **authored inside CRETA** by a controller and exported to SAP — SAP is a downstream target, never a source (`[F-DIR-01]`); UM figures are integers (`[F-UM-01]`) and the snapshot reads the **active** UM version for the period. Lines are read-only and normalised to 100. The editor shows the **Refresh from UM** button to re-snapshot when a newer UM version is activated; a dry-run dialog with Added / Removed / Changed sections previews the diff before commit. *(The InternalService Stage-2 collapse — an internal service's spread becoming a pure derived view of UM — is a later cluster; this describes current Project/Offering behaviour.)*

**Mode change per `[F-S2-05]`:** the **Switch to manual** / **Switch to automatic** button gates a confirmation dialog showing the current values. Manual → automatic warns the user the manual values will be discarded and asks for the S-code; automatic → manual inherits the snapshot verbatim and unlocks the line editor.

**Year rollover per `[F-S2-07]`:** the New profile dialog has a **Copy from…** tab. Pick a source profile (any year), pick a target year + entity, and the lines copy verbatim. Mode is preserved. Lineage is recorded via `copied_from_profile_id`. A bulk endpoint (`POST /api/admin/btc-profiles/year-rollover`) processes all active profiles in one shot for annual planning kickoff.

**Sandbox mode per `[B-OQ-02]`:** when the simulator's CostAllocationSurface mounts the same editor for a Lever 12 scenario, the canonical UM-refresh and mode-switch buttons hide; line edits route through `ScenarioContext.setBtcLines()` instead of writing to the canonical `BTCProfileLine` rows. Only **Promote** (W06.5) materialises the scenario overlay onto canonical state.

sections.title: Location Cost Rollup
sections.body:
**Purpose:** show the magnitude of Stage 2 charge by geography in a single map view, and let the user drill from region down to charging location and on into the upstream chain.

**Two sub-views, single tab pair:**
- **Map view** — static SVG world map (no tile service per spec), country-level bubbles by default. Bubble size = total € (square-root scale clamped to [4, 28]); bubble colour = dominant division for the country (Corporate IT blue, Truck & Bus amber, Rail Vehicle emerald, other neutral). Hover reveals a popup with the entity-level breakdown; click a country to drill into per-charging-location bubbles around the country centroid; click a location bubble to open a side panel with the per-location breakdown (total cost, legal entities operating at the location as an informational chip list, and chargeable-entity inflows with Amount + Share %). Map state is preserved underneath the panel so several locations can be drilled in succession.
- **Tree table** — Region → Country → Charging location → Entity. Each row expandable; leaf rows show the entity's Stage 2 € for the selected (year, version). Clicking a charging-location row drills further into the upstream chain (which entities contributed to that location's amount).

**Why legal entities don't carry their own cost split:** BTC Stage 2 splits to a charging location, and one charging location commonly hosts several legal entities (e.g. `cl-de-muc` has 4: LE-DE-001..004). The data model has no per-LE allocation rule, so legal entities appear in the level-4 panel as informational metadata rather than as a cost-split level.

**Caching:** the rollup is backed by `RollupCache` keyed by `(cache_layer, year, version, key_id)` for `stage1_effective` and `stage2_location` layers. Distribution writes invalidate the year+version slice for both layers; BTC writes invalidate the entity's stage2 entries; entity `annual_cost` writes invalidate both layers for the entity. Controllers can manually flush via `POST /api/admin/rollup-cache/invalidate` and inspect cache state at `GET /api/admin/rollup-cache/status`.

**Quarterly drill-down per `[F-RV-06]`:** the forecast lifecycle is annual; the version selector exposes the only quarterly affordance (snapshots are taken per cycle close). Deeper time slicing (per-month) lives in the Workbench and is not part of the rollup.

sections.title: Reporting bridge
sections.body:
**Purpose:** since the standard Report Builder doesn't yet have a native Cluster F data source (open note in `[F-RV-04]`), the fourth sidebar section is a discoverability bridge into the AI Report Builder. Three quick-prompt buttons jump straight to `/reporting/builder?prompt=<prefilled>`:
- **Cost by division** → 'Show me total annual effective cost by charging location for 2026, broken down by division.'
- **Top inflow drivers** → 'Top 10 chargeable entities by inflow total in 2026 — surface the ones whose effective cost is dominated by upstream services.'
- **Regional YoY** → 'Compare 2025 vs 2026 effective cost by region for all chargeable entities; highlight regions with > 10% growth.'

Below the hero card a catalogue lists the 11 dimensions (entity / entity_type / hierarchy_node / responsible / change_or_run / charging_location / legal_entity / region / division / country / pipeline_stage) and 6 measures (effective_cost / own_cost / inflow_total / stage2_amount / to_business_pct / self_retained_pct) the Cluster F data layer exposes.

sections.title: Role-based access summary
sections.body:
Per `[F-AC-01]`, edit gates apply per-entity-type:
- **Distribution edges** — controllers can edit any; non-controllers need an explicit `RolePermissionGrant` on `entity_type='distribution'`. Reads open to all roles.
- **BTC profiles** — same pattern (`entity_type='btc_profile'`), additionally with the responsible person on the entity holding the canonical role-default per `[F-AC-01]`.
- **Location Cost Rollup** — read-only for everyone; no role gate.
- **Reporting bridge** — read-only; downstream Report Builder applies its own role-based data scoping.

Grants are managed under Administration → Role Permissions per `[F-AC-01]`; the Audit Log records every grant change under category `access_control`.

sections.title: Effective-dated versioning and the simulator overlay
sections.body:
**Stage 1 (FD-3):** distribution edges are organised into `DistributionVersion` headers with per-version `active_from` dates. The in-force production version on any date is the one with the latest `active_from ≤ that date`. There is no `baseline` / `forecast` / `actuals` string axis on Stage 1 — that v4 holdover was removed in the FD-3 rework. Forecast-cycle reproducibility (when needed) is provided by the immutability guarantee on activated versions: once `status='active'`, the header and its edges cannot be mutated; re-entry creates a new draft that, on activation, becomes the new in-force version.

**Scenario forks per `[F-S1-02]`:** the What-If simulator's lever 12 creates a dedicated `DistributionVersion` per scenario (discriminated by `scenario_id`, kept at `status='draft'` permanently). Lazy-fork at the edge level: only entities the user actually touches get scenario edges; union-aware reads fall back to the anchor production version's edges for untouched sources. Scenario versions are excluded from production resolution — they are not visited by `active_from` lookup.

**Scenario anchor pinning:** at scenario creation, `Scenario.anchor_distribution_version_id` is pinned to the production version in force on that date. Subsequent production-version activations do not shift the scenario's impact deltas — the user keeps comparing against the same anchor they started with. Legacy scenarios with NULL anchors fall back to resolve-by-date-at-read-time.

**Stage 2 BTC profiles** are *not* versioned the same way; scenario edits to BTC line percentages are stored as `ScenarioAction` overlays on the scenario rather than copied into a sandbox `BTCProfile` row. At impact-preview time the impact-calc service merges the overlay with the canonical profile to produce the scenario view; Promote copies overlay values onto the live `BTCProfileLine` rows.

**Cleanup:** deleting a scenario removes its scenario-scoped `DistributionVersion` row (cascade removes its edges) AND its BTC `ScenarioAction` overlays in one pass via `services/scenario_lever12.cleanup_lever12_state`.
